input.strategy_title: Integrated GenAI model evaluation for RHOAI
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers adopting generative models on RHOAI have no supported way to answer
"is this model good enough for my use case?" inside the platform. Evaluation
today happens in ad-hoc notebooks with lm-evaluation-harness or vendor tools,
results live in spreadsheets, and nothing links an evaluation to the model
version that was actually deployed. We need a first-class evaluation capability:
run standard and custom benchmarks against models served on the platform,
persist results alongside the model version, and let users compare candidates
before promoting one to production.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | Users can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite. |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Standard benchmark suites (e.g. MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag exposed through lm-eval task names) are available out of the box. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | Evaluation results are persisted and linked to the Model Registry version of the evaluated model. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Users can define custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics) and run them through the same flow. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | The Dashboard shows evaluation runs, their status, and per-benchmark scores, and allows side-by-side comparison of two model versions. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | Evaluations can be embedded as a step in a Data Science Pipeline so promotion flows can gate on scores. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Llama Stack's eval provider API is backed by the platform evaluation service, so agents/apps built on Llama Stack get the same results. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Evaluation runs record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) for capacity planning. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Product documentation covers the evaluation workflow end to end, including custom task authoring. |

## Affected Components

- TrustyAI
- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry

## Out of Scope

- Human-preference (arena style) evaluation collection
- Automatic model promotion decisions — pipelines gate, humans promote
- Fine-tuning feedback loops driven by evaluation scores

## Open Questions

1. Execution engine: TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (Tech Preview) already wraps
   lm-evaluation-harness — do we build on it as the single execution path, or is
   a new evaluation service needed to also serve Llama Stack's eval provider
   API? Needs a technical investigation with a recommendation.
2. Result schema: what is the canonical result format persisted to Model
   Registry custom properties, and does it survive benchmark-suite version
   bumps? Prototype against real MMLU output before committing.
3. Benchmark dataset licensing: which standard suites can we redistribute in
   disconnected environments, and which must be fetched by the customer?

# Extend LMEvalJob into the supported evaluation execution path (Outcome A)

## Description

If the execution-engine investigation recommends building on TrustyAI's
LMEvalJob, extend it from Tech Preview into the supported platform
evaluation execution capability: launching evaluations of models served on
the platform, standard benchmark suites out of the box, and cost/duration
metadata capture. This epic exists only if that investigation selects the
extend-LMEvalJob outcome. Result persistence to Model Registry and custom
evaluation task support are additive capabilities on this execution flow and
are delivered by separate epics under the same outcome, so this epic stays a
single-sprint unit and the lower-priority custom-task work can be deferred
independently.

## Scope

- Extend the LMEvalJob path so an evaluation can target a model served on the
  platform — a KServe InferenceService endpoint or a Llama Stack
  distribution — against a selected benchmark suite.
- Deliver standard benchmark suites (e.g., MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag via lm-eval
  task names) out of the box, using the per-suite delivery mechanism decided
  by the benchmark licensing analysis (bundled vs. documented customer fetch).
- Record cost/duration metadata per run (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) in the
  run's result record, per the field definitions of the canonical result
  schema.
- Emit completed runs' result records — per-benchmark scores and cost/duration
  metadata — conforming to the canonical result schema, available to the
  result-persistence capability delivered under the same outcome.
- Promote the capability from Tech Preview to supported: stable CRD fields,
  documented upgrade path, backward compatibility with existing Tech Preview
  usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe
  endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite.
- Standard suites are available out of the box per the benchmark licensing
  allowlist produced by the licensing analysis; the suite-delivery scope of
  this epic (which suites ship bundled vs. via documented customer fetch) is
  finalized against that allowlist before the epic is complete. Suites that
  cannot be redistributed have a documented customer-fetch path.
- Each run records cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) in
  its result record per the canonical result schema.
- Completed runs emit result records — per-benchmark scores and cost/duration
  metadata — conforming to the canonical evaluation result schema, available
  to the result-persistence capability delivered under the same outcome.
- Existing Tech Preview LMEvalJob usage keeps working: CRD changes are
  backward compatible or ship with a documented migration (rollback/compat
  plan per the replaces-existing-capability rule).

## HLR Traceability

HLR-1 (launch evaluations), HLR-2 (standard suites out of the box), HLR-8
(cost/duration metadata capture; schema fields defined by the result-schema
investigation). HLR-3 (persistence write path) and HLR-4 (custom evaluation
tasks) are delivered by separate epics under the extend-LMEvalJob outcome.

# Persist evaluation results to Model Registry (Outcome A)

## Description

Under the extend-LMEvalJob outcome, persist the evaluation results produced by
the supported execution path and link them to the Model Registry version of
the evaluated model, using the canonical result schema through the Model
Registry REST API custom properties. This epic exists only if the
execution-engine investigation selects the extend-LMEvalJob outcome. The
write path is carved out of the execution epic so it can be delivered and
reviewed as a single-sprint unit.

## Scope

- Write path from the extended LMEvalJob execution flow to Model Registry:
  when an evaluation run completes, its results are persisted and linked to
  the Model Registry version of the evaluated model.
- Persisted payloads conform to the canonical evaluation result schema,
  including per-benchmark scores and cost/duration metadata (schema fields
  defined by the result-schema investigation).
- Use the documented Model Registry extension point only — ModelVersion
  custom properties via the REST API; no private component APIs.
- Stay consistent with the Model Registry team's formal validation of the
  custom-properties round-trip (field type/size limits, version-bump
  resilience): the write path must satisfy the validated limits rather than
  re-deriving them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Results of an evaluation run — per-benchmark scores and cost/duration
  metadata — are persisted and linked to the evaluated model's Model Registry
  version per the canonical result schema.
- Persisted results round-trip through the Model Registry REST API consistent
  with the owning team's validation conclusions (type/size limits,
  version-bump resilience).
- No private Model Registry APIs are used — custom properties via the
  documented REST extension point only.

## HLR Traceability

HLR-3 (evaluation results persisted and linked to the Model Registry version
of the evaluated model) — write path under the extend-LMEvalJob outcome.

# Custom evaluation task support (Outcome A)

## Description

Under the extend-LMEvalJob outcome, let users define custom evaluation tasks
— their own datasets and metrics — and run them through the same execution
flow as the standard benchmark suites. This epic exists only if the
execution-engine investigation selects the extend-LMEvalJob outcome. Custom
task support is an additive P1 capability on the execution flow and is carved
into its own epic so it can be planned and deferred independently of the P0
execution and persistence work.

## Scope

- A task-definition surface for the extended LMEvalJob path: users supply
  their own datasets and metrics as an evaluation task.
- Custom tasks execute through the same flow as standard suites — same
  launch path, same run resource, no parallel execution mechanism.
- Custom-task results use the canonical result schema and the same
  persistence path as standard-suite runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can define a custom evaluation task (own dataset and metrics) and
  run it against a model served on the platform through the same flow used
  for standard benchmark suites.
- Custom-task runs produce results in the canonical result schema and are
  persisted and linked to the evaluated model's Model Registry version
  identically to standard-suite runs.
- No parallel execution path exists for custom tasks — they reuse the
  standard execution, result, and persistence flow.

## HLR Traceability

HLR-4 (users can define custom evaluation tasks — own datasets and metrics —
and run them through the same flow), under the extend-LMEvalJob outcome.
